<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />and {{GHGheb|text=פַּרַד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=19}} f.); in a few verbs also ''Pilpēl'' ({{GHGpar|55|f}}) is found, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גִּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll}}, ''Hithpalpēl'' {{GHGheb|text=הִתְגַּלְגֵּל|translate=to roll oneself}} (from {{GHGheb|text=גָּלַל}}); imperative with suffix {{GHGheb|text=סַלְסְלֶהָ|translate=exalt her}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=4|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁעֲשַׁע|translate=to comfort, to delight in}}; passive {{GHGheb|text=שָֽׁעֳשַׁע|translate=to be caressed}} (from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁעַע}}). These forms cannot appear in a biliteral form any more than {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}; cf. {{GHGheb|text=עִוְעִים}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=14}}) and {{GHGheb|text=קַוְקָו}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=2.7}}).—For {{GHGheb|text=תִּתָּבָר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=27}} read, according to {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְבָּרָר}}.

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks}}

I. ''On Qal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|m}}
1. In the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, isolated examples are found with ''ō'' in the first syllable, which it is customary to refer to triliteral stems with middle ''ō'' (like {{GHGheb|text=יָכֹל}}, {{GHGpar|43|a}}); viz. {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫מּוּ|translate=they are exalted}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=24}} to {{GHGheb|text=רָמֹם}}; {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫בּוּ|translate=they shot}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=23}} to {{GHGheb|text=רָבֹב}}; {{GHGheb|text=זֹ֫רוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=6}} to {{GHGheb|text=זָרֹר}}. But this explanation is very doubtful: {{GHGheb|text=זֹ֫רוּ}} especially is rather to be classed among the passives of Qal mentioned in {{GHGpar|52|e}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|n}}
2. ''Imperfects Qal'' with ''ō'' in the second syllable keep the original ''a'' in the preformative, but lengthen it to ''ā'', as being in an open syllable, hence {{GHGheb|text=יָחֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָמֹד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָעֹז}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֹן}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֹעַ}} (trans. ''he breaks in pieces'', but {{GHGheb|text=יֵרַע}} intrans.= ''he is evil''); imperfects with ''ă'' have, in the preformative, an ''ē'', lengthened from ''ĭ''. See the examples below, under p, {{GHGpar|63|c}} and e, {{GHGpar|72|h}}, and specially Barth in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1894, p. 5 f.

The ''Ḥōlĕm'' of the ''infinitive, imperative'', and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} ({{GHGheb|text=סֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}}) is only tone-long, and therefore, as a rule, is written defectively (with a few exceptions, chiefly in the later orthography, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צוֹר|translate=bind up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹם}} ver. 7; {{GHGheb|text=לָבֽוֹז}} for {{GHGheb|text=לָבֹז|translate=to plunder}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=8|verse=11|hidebook=1}}). When this ''ō'' loses the tone, it becomes in the final syllable ''ŏ'', in a sharpened syllable ''ŭ'', or not infrequently even ''ŏ'' (see above, k). Examples of ''ŏ'' are: (''a'') in a toneless final syllable, i.e. before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} or in the {{GHGterm|imperfect consecutive}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָן־}} (''rŏn'') ''to rejoice'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫סָב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18}} (once even with ''ŭ'' in a toneless final syllable, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫רֻם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=20}}); on the other hand, in the ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּסֹ֫בּוּ}}, {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}; (''b'') before a tone-bearing ''afformative'' or ''suffix'', e.g. ''imperative 2nd sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=רָנִּ֫י}}, {{GHGheb|text=גָּזִּ֫י}} (cf. ff); {{GHGheb|text=חָנֵּ֫נִי|translate=pity me}}; {{GHGheb|text=סָלּ֫וּהָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְשָׁדֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=11|verse=3}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGheb|text=תְּחָגֻּֽהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=14}} (for the defective writing, cf. {{GHGheb|text=יְסֻבֻּ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=40|verse=22}}). In {{GHGheb|text=יָחְנְךָ֫}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=19}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִחָנְךָ}}) this ''ŏ'' is thrown back to the preformative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|o}}
On the 2nd plur. fem. imperat. {{GHGheb|text=עֹ֫רָה|translate=make yourselves naked}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=11}}, cf. the analogous forms in {{GHGpar|48|i}}.—Quite abnormal is the {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} {{GHGheb|text=רֹ֫עָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=24|verse=19}} (as {{GHGheb|text=ה}} follows, probably only a case of dittography for {{GHGheb|text=רֹעַ}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=קֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}} and {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=2|verse=16}}); so also are the ''imperatives'' {{GHGheb|text=קָֽבָה־לִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=11.17}}, and {{GHGheb|text=אָֽרָה־לִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, with {{GHGheb|text=ה|translate=paragogic}}. We should expect {{GHGheb|text=קֻ֫בָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫רָה}}. If these forms are to be read ''qŏballî, ʾŏrallî'', they would be analogous to such cases as {{GHGheb|text=מִדְבַּ֫רָה}} ({{GHGpar|90|i}}), the addition of the {{GHGterm|paragogic}} {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} causing no change in the form of the word ({{GHGheb|text=קָב־}} like {{GHGheb|text=רָן־}} above). If, however, as Jewish tradition requires, they are to be read ''qāballî, ʾārallî'', then in both cases the {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} must be explained, with<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
